conviction_note: Three small positive sourced findings: zinc at a 4-year high flowing into surcharges while kettle cost lags 6-8 months, AHRI HVAC shipments +20-22% y/y in June-July against a Precoat HVAC decline in Q1, and Valmont Coatings +17% / NA Utility +34% reported after AZZ last spoke. Each sits inside a consensus that already assumes ~+10-11% revenue growth and a guide that already embeds it. Against a +10 vol-point put skew and a stock that sold its July beat-and-raise (-1.88%), that gives p_up 54 on an abs move of 6.5, so +0.52 scaled. The findings sum to +1.05; the gap is the reaction function and the skew, which the scaled number carries and the findings do not.

positioning_check: Short interest is about 3.1-3.2% of float with 2.2-2.6 days to cover (Benzinga, 2026-06-30 settlement; CurvedTrading/FINRA, 2026-07-15 settlement: about 1.0M shares, 2.6 DTC). Run-up is +3.76% over 20 days and -2.47% over 5 days, 13.8% below the 52-week high. Sources: https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/AZZ/short-interest and https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/azz/short-interest/

findings.finding: LME zinc rose through fiscal Q2 (Jun-Aug) to a 4-year high, with cash settlement at $4,107/t on 2026-08-27, up 55% from its mid-2025 trough. On the July call AZZ said surcharges flow through sales at current zinc levels while zinc bought today reaches the kettles 6-8 months later. That points to surcharge-lifted Metal Coatings sales and a margin tailwind in the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 Metal Coatings sales +12.3% with margin down 260bp (30.3%); the stock fell 1.88% on that beat-and-raise. The Q2 FY26 EPS miss ($1.55 vs $1.57) drew -4.9%. Metal Coatings margin has been the swing line.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue of $458-462M (+10-11% y/y) sits on the FY guide set on 2026-07-08, before the late-August zinc spike. If the surcharge effect were priced, estimates would have moved up after August and the skew would not be +10 to the downside. It is partly priced: zinc is public, and a cost that lags its price is the company's stated mechanism, not a measured number. The same spike raises H2/FY28 kettle costs, which could temper the forward commentary.
findings.independence: Mechanism from the Q1 FY27 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/AZZ/Q12027): surcharges stay at current levels, zinc reaches the kettles 6-8 months later, and surcharges are being added in Precoat too. Price path also from Trading Economics, 2026-09-07: $3,986/t, +38.5% over 12 months (https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/zinc/news/581689).

findings.finding: AHRI US central AC and heat-pump shipments rose 21.7% y/y in June 2026 and 20.1% in July 2026, after AZZ reported Precoat HVAC/appliance volume down 2.4% in fiscal Q1 (Mar-May). That points to a better HVAC volume line in Precoat for Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Precoat volume weakness (-4.3% sales) came with the Q2 FY26 miss and the -4.9% reaction. Q1 FY27 Precoat was +1.5%, with no visible effect on the -1.88% move.
findings.why_not_priced: Published after AZZ last spoke, and nobody models AZZ off AHRI. If it were priced, Precoat estimates would have moved up from the flat-to-low-single-digit growth the July call implied. Net of the rest of the company, HVAC is only a slice of Precoat (about 53% of sales), the comparison is easy (June-July 2025 were very weak), and construction is the larger Precoat end market and was soft in Q1. So this is a small proxy finding.
findings.independence: June figures from ACHR News / refindustry (https://refindustry.com/?p=78906), which is the same AHRI series. No company or counterparty confirmation.

findings.finding: Valmont's Q2 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-27, reported 2026-07-21, after AZZ's July 8 call) showed Coatings +17% and North America Utility +34%, a raised full-year guide, and a utility/data-center cycle it called early-stage. This supports galvanizing volume in AZZ's Jun-Aug quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Metal Coatings volume beats (Q1 FY27 +12.3%, Q4 FY26) drew -1.88% and +8.66%. The reaction is inconsistent.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print that landed after AZZ spoke. But consensus already assumes about +10-11% total growth, and AZZ itself said on 2026-07-09 that Q2 'got off to a really good start'. If it were unpriced, Q2 estimates would sit at the guide midpoint pace rather than above it; they sit roughly at it. So this is mostly inside guidance.
findings.independence: AZZ Q1 FY27 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/AZZ/Q12027): data centers are the fastest-growing construction area and most plants have a data-center project. The company's own commentary points the same way, so this is partly the same story.

findings.finding: AZZ bought Seattle Galvanizing (two Seattle-area plants, more than 50,000 tons a year of capacity, 43 sites after the deal) on 2026-07-30, inside Q2. That adds about one month of revenue, and AZZ called the deal accretive within the first year. Guidance excludes M&A.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to a bolt-on on a print.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public. Because guidance excludes M&A, the guide may be raised mechanically for it. It is small: roughly $15-25M of annual revenue at typical galvanizing pricing, which is an inference, since terms were not disclosed.

findings.finding: On the July call management said it 'would anticipate being in the market to buy some shares back' if the stock stayed in its range, with $133.2M of authorization left. The stock traded at about $137 in mid-September, near the July range, so a Q2 repurchase disclosure is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. No buybacks in Q1 FY27.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a stated intention, not a disclosed action. If buying had been heavy it would show in the 10-Q share count, which is unseen until tonight. Small.
findings.independence: Bullstory snapshot of 2026-09-12 has the price at $137.07 (https://bullstory.io/en/stocks/azz/forecast/price-target).

findings.finding: Two insiders sold after the July print: director Jeffrey Vellines (Form 144 and Form 4, 2026-08-11) and Bryan Stovall (Form 144 and Form 4, 2026-08-14). There were no insider purchases in the window.
findings.why_not_priced: These are routine-looking post-print sales by two people, visible on EDGAR. They carry little signal and are filed small because the core says file them.

rejected_candidates.detail: The Metal Coatings volume read is already carried by the Valmont Coatings/Utility finding. A steel-price guide adds no AZZ-specific line, and Precoat largely tolls customer substrate.

rejected_candidates.detail: It is wire-level sentiment that is already in the price, not a fact about the print. It is used as the price reference in the buyback finding.

baseline_tension: What I found leans mildly positive against a +10 vol-point downside skew, a +3.8% 20-day run-up and a name that sold its last beat-and-raise. I cannot say why the option market is wrong about this print, so p_up stays at 54.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; the July beat-and-raise fell 1.88%): the reported-quarter findings shrank. Zinc went from +0.5 to +0.4, HVAC from +0.4 to +0.25, Valmont from +0.4 to +0.3.

Lesson 6 (inside guidance): the Valmont and HVAC findings land inside the FY guide's implied ~+10% growth and the consensus built on it, which is part of the cut above. The bar is sourced to three agreeing estimate sources, so there is no cap.
Lesson 7 (sign against a +10 skew with no reason the options are wrong): p_up went from 55 to 54, so the scaled number moved from +0.65 to +0.52.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the HVAC finding is sized net of the larger, softer construction part of Precoat and of Metal Coatings.
The Seattle, buyback and insider findings were left unchanged.
